derivations.claim: Quaternion conjugation preserves the imaginary subspace and norm, is a homomorphism into SO(3), and is onto by the axis-angle representation.
The kernel is {1,-1}; the differential is the isomorphism v -> (x -> [v,x]); and the cross-product Lie algebra is nonabelian and simple.
SU(2) has center {1,-1}, SO(3) has trivial center, and the groups are distinct compact global forms with isomorphic simple Lie algebras.
A result at G=SU(2) is one instance and does not discharge the separate G=SO(3) case of the universal group claim.

finite_checks: For q=1 and q=-1, conjugation fixes every imaginary quaternion.
For unit n and q=cos(theta/2)+n sin(theta/2), quaternion multiplication gives rotation by theta; theta=0 gives the identity and theta=pi gives the half-turn about n.
The basis brackets [i,j]=2k, [j,k]=2i, and [k,i]=2j show the nonabelian cross-product structure used in the ideal argument.

derivations.claim: The plaquette product lies in SU(2), its real trace lies in [-2,2], and the Wilson action lies in [0,2 beta].
Left and right multiplication preserve the round volume on SU(2), so the normalized link measure is invariant and its fourfold product has total mass one.
Integrating the pointwise exponential bounds against the finite probability measure gives e^(-2 beta) <= Z_beta <= 1 and Z_0=1.
The finite graph integral specifies no continuum fields, continuum limit, reconstructed Hilbert space, or Hamiltonian and therefore establishes no Clay mass-gap result.

finite_checks: At beta=0 the integrand is one everywhere and the normalized measure gives Z_0=1.
If all four links are the identity, U_p=I and the action is zero.
The assignment U_1=-I and U_2=U_3=U_4=I gives U_p=-I and action 2 beta; this attains the lower pointwise weight e^(-2 beta), not necessarily the integral lower bound.
